analysisResults:
The system continues to provide significant value to the exporting community.  Current FY 2020 and FY 2021 Metrics meet customer and financial goals with results representing effectiveness of program as a measure of user efficiency and customer shipping authorizations (aka validations). Validations are license decisions determined and issued by BIS. It has immediate impact on customer satisfaction as it determines what, where, and when for exporting conditions if approved. An ineffective technical licensing posture would impact global exports of licensed products, weaken the collaborative inter-agency license adjudication process, and cause additional storage cost and lost revenue to American businesses. BIS is also measuring those activities that are important and help satisfy other federal mandates, like security assessments and vulnerability monitoring.
In FY 2020, BIS processed 37,895 export license applications, via the CUESS application suite, with a total value of $173.7 billion. This marked a 10.8% increase from the 34,207 applications processed in 2019. BIS approved 32,687 license applications (86.3%), returned 4,754 applications without action (12.5%), and denied 454 applications (1.2%). The BIS average license application processing time this year was 23 days. This included time for reviews by the Departments of Defense, Energy, and State. Of FY 2020 licenses, Export Control Classification Number (ECCN) 9A610 (military aircraft and related commodities) was the greatest number of approved applications (4,994 licenses valued at a total of $14.7 billion). ECCN 5A992 (information security equipment) was the dual-use ECCN with the highest total value of approved applications ($21.2 billion involving 173 license approvals). BIS added 279 entities to the Entity List via nine Final Rules .
For FY 2020, U.S. companies exported $6.35 billion of licensed items. BIS-licensed exports represented 0.4% of total U.S. exports. Exports made under a BIS license exception totaled $14.5 billion, representing approximately 1.0% of overall U.S. exports.

Future Outlook
Beginning in FY 2022, BIS plans to initiate modernization efforts to redesign the CUESS suite of applications using native cloud-based technologies

The Bureau of Industry and Security (BIS) is a part of the United States Department of Commerce that sits at the intersection of multiple federal agency partners (Department of State, Department of Justice, Department of Homeland Security, Department of the Treasury, NASA, the Intelligence Community) and orchestrates and enforces the nation’s Export Administration Regulations (EAR) and other export control legal requirements. BIS has a key role, within the context of a whole of government approach in addressing the threats of our foreign adversaries including diversion of dual use technologies to military uses; theft of intellectual property; human rights abuses; and anti-competitive, unfair and coercive trade practices.

There is a mission-critical need for BIS to better coordinate and exchange data including license applicants and potential export violators with our US government partners, but also to develop advanced data sharing and analytics capabilities with our international partners such as Canada and the European Union.

In FY24, we are building on this foundation by enhancing application security, starting with Simplified Network Application Process Redesign (SNAP-R).  Additionally, the CIO office has embraced a user-centric design approach that engages CUESS application users, gathering valuable insights and feedback in order to improve application design and enhance user experience.

analysisResults: SEVIS is utilized as a critical national security database. It originated as an immigration benefits tracking tool, but throughout its existence, it has been adapted to the ever-growing needs of its users. It is now regarded as a primary resource for conducting threat analysis for counterterrorism and/or counterintelligence by the law enforcement and intelligence communities. In response to the 14 February 2013 DHS Acquisition Decision Memorandum, ICE completed system vulnerability mitigation to 75% by the end of FY16. The completed?Analysis of Alternatives, which was confirmed by the SEVIS Modernization Oversight Board on 14 January 2016, identified the most appropriate course of action for the resolution of remaining known system vulnerabilities and sustainability of system performance. In May of 2019, the DHS Acquisition Review Board determined that the program had sufficiently mitigated the remaining vulnerabilities through a combination of functional and process improvements, and the program received approval for Final Operating Capability (FOC) on May 29, 2019.? The program was tasked with resolving the outstanding person-centric vulnerability, which it has done by successfully implementing matching algorithms in the database.The program successfully mitigated the person-centric vulnerability in the database and is continuing to refine the matching.? algorithms.?Additional federal staff have been hired to fill resource shortfalls previously identified.? However, due to revenue/funding issues, the program has not been able to backfill two FTE positions initially identified through the staffing analysis since those positions were vacated.

The RVSS-U continues to meet the operators’ needs, providing the functionality and performance to help them in deterrence, detecting and tracking, IoI identification, and BPA situational awareness and response. 
  
 Strategic and Business Results:
 The RVSS-U located throughout southern Arizona and parts of RGV, combined with relocatable systems, is helping to prevent illegal import/entry and export/exit as described in the CBP Vision and Strategy 2020. DEERS is a comprehensive central repository of Department of Defense (DoD) Human Resource information, including the eight Uniformed Services, retirees, family members, civilian personnel, contractors, Veterans and others. DEERS is the authoritative source for DoD identity management and services including personnel and family relationships; national security clearances; verification of military service and employment; official strength accounting for manpower planning, deployment and contingency; and occupational health. DEERS provides benefits determination, including education, life insurance, financial protections, and healthcare eligibility and enrollment.?

?

DEERS creates and manages the DoD Identification Number (DoD ID) to ensure accurate data is shared across services, supporting Common Access Card (CAC) issuance, personnel accountability, testing and recruiting, and the transitional assistance management program. DEERS provides authoritative personnel identification, validation and authentication for DoD agencies, the Uniformed Services, the Veteran?s Administration, the US Department of Labor, the US Department of Education, the US Department of Health and Human Services, the Department of Commerce, the Internal Revenue Service, the Federal Bureau of Investigation, the Department of Justice, the Office of Personnel Management, the Transportation Security Administration, the Office of Management and Budget, the Congressional Budget Office, State VA Agencies, State Medicaid, Department of Justice, and the US Congress.?

?

While hundreds of DoD capabilities rely on DEERS for day-to-day operations, the underlying system structures are dated, depending on large amounts of non-integrated data, obtained from multiple sources, in various formats, with different reporting frequencies and levels of quality. DEERS stores more than 50 million records on individuals with current or past DoD affiliations across 160 distinct databases to support various business capabilities. Consolidating external business lines has further increased duplicate data, as will the Veterans Administration use of DoD?s electronic health record, MHS GENESIS; this will require DEERS to absorb ~40 million VA patients into its databases and assume identity management functions for VA.  Such expanded requirements will necessitate enhancements to ensure that DEERS data is more visible, more accessible, more understandable, more trusted, and more interoperable in the future.?

Three years ago, EDCAPS systems began migrating from aging IBM servers running on the AIX operating system to less expensive DELL X86 servers running the Red Hat Linux operating system three years ago. As of June 30, EPA no longer accepts manifest submissions through the mail.

Communications prior to system launch and the early years focused on transitioning receiving  facility submission methods from mail to methods where they upload the paper manifest into the system.

Mailed paper manifests submissions have been decreasing steadily. EPA has been directly working with facilities still mailing in June 2021 in order to transition to fully electronic manifesting and other submission options.

agencyName: Department of Health and Human Services
investmentTitle: CMS Healthcare Integrated General Ledger Accounting System (HIGLAS)
analysisResults:
CMS’ Healthcare Integrated General Ledger Accounting System (HIGLAS) is a single, integrated dual-entry accounting system that standardizes and centralizes Federal financial accounting functions for CMS’ programs.  HIGLAS, CMS’s financial system of record began operation in 2005 and reduced over 50 legacy financial systems and reporting entities for Medicare, Administrative Program Accounting (APA), Benefits/Medicare Secondary Payer Recovery Contractor (MSPRC), the Center for Consumer Information and Insurance Oversight (CCIIO), and the Railroad Retirement (RRB) into one consolidated general ledger system.  The main objective of this effort was to leverage the use of commercial off the shelf (COTS) software in the federal government to increase automation and efficiency, and to maximize economies of effort to centralize management and save millions of taxpayer dollars that fund Medicare and Medicaid each year, while at the same time eliminating redundant and inefficient/ineffective manual processes. CMS'  implementation of HIGLAS was a strategic improvement and modernization effort of the Agency’s accounting systems, financial management, and internal controls.  The HIGLAS initiative accomplished:
-        The establishment of an integrated general ledger accounting system, maintaining the detailed financial transactional data of every Medicare Administrative Contractor (MACs) in the CMS financial system of record to be compliant with reporting standards.
-        The replacement of CMS’s legacy accounting system of record, the Financial Accounting Control System (FACS).
HIGLAS, a mission critical system, enables CMS to manage program accounting for its business operations. On an average, HIGLAS processes 4.1 million claims daily accounting for approximately $2.2 trillion in annual payment transactions thus making it the largest Oracle Federal Financials System.  HIGLAS continues to enhance CMS’s oversight of financial operations, in order to achieve reliable, audit-able, timely financial accounting, and reporting for CMS’s programs and activities. The HIGLAS effort has significantly improved the ability of CMS/HHS to perform accounting transactions. These improvements and benefits attributable to HIGLAS include reduced costs due to elimination of redundant individual Medicare financial record systems, improvements in automated Medicare debt collection/referral activities, creation of audit trails for every Medicare transaction/payment/claim in HIGLAS.

analysisResults:
The 2018-2022 and 2023-2027 NSDUH contracts include survey redesign tasks purposed for the likely implementation during a future NSDUH survey year. Some of these redesign tasks do involve IT Development, Modernization, and Enhancement (DME) activities. These DME (as well as O&M) costs are reflected in the quarterly FITARA cost worksheet submitted to SAMHSA DTM. 
The mission of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is to reduce the impact of substance abuse and mental illness on America's communities.  To accomplish its work, SAMHSA administers a combination of competitive, formula, and block grant programs and data collection activities. Within SAMHSA, the following Centers administer and manage the various programs and data collection activities: the Center for Mental Health Services (CMHS); the Center for Substance Abuse Prevention (CSAP); the Center for Substance Abuse Treatment (CSAT); and the Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality (CBHSQ).   Part of CBHSQ's mission includes the collection, analysis, and dissemination of national and state level behavioral health data on substance use and mental health, related health conditions, the supply and utilization of behavioral health services, the operation of behavioral health services in specialty and primary care facilities, costs of behavioral health care, service utilization, and changes in behavioral health outcomes.  The National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) is sponsored by SAMHSA and is managed by CBHSQ.  The NSDUH provides data on the incidence and prevalence of substance use and mental illness as required by Section 505 of the Public Health Service Act (42 USC 290aa4).  Conducted on a periodic basis from 1971 through 1988, and annually since 1990, the NSDUH provides current data on substance use and mental health for the U.S. civilian, non-institutionalized population aged 12 or older.  Since 1999 NSDUH has provided data for each State and the District of Columbia.  Section 505 of the Public Health Service Act requires that these data must be collected annually.

analysisResults:
The 2018-2022 and 2023-2027 NSDUH contracts include survey redesign tasks purposed for the likely implementation during a future NSDUH survey year. Some of these redesign tasks do involve IT Development, Modernization, and Enhancement (DME) activities. These DME (as well as O&M) costs are reflected in the quarterly FITARA cost worksheet submitted to SAMHSA DTM. 
The mission of the Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (SAMHSA) of the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) is to reduce the impact of substance abuse and mental illness on America's communities.  To accomplish its work, SAMHSA administers a combination of competitive, formula, and block grant programs and data collection activities. Within SAMHSA, the following Centers administer and manage the various programs and data collection activities: the Center for Mental Health Services (CMHS); the Center for Substance Abuse Prevention (CSAP); the Center for Substance Abuse Treatment (CSAT); and the Center for Behavioral Health Statistics and Quality (CBHSQ).   Part of CBHSQ's mission includes the collection, analysis, and dissemination of national and state level behavioral health data on substance use and mental health, related health conditions, the supply and utilization of behavioral health services, the operation of behavioral health services in specialty and primary care facilities, costs of behavioral health care, service utilization, and changes in behavioral health outcomes.  The National Survey on Drug Use and Health (NSDUH) is sponsored by SAMHSA and is managed by CBHSQ.  The NSDUH provides data on the incidence and prevalence of substance use and mental illness as required by Section 505 of the Public Health Service Act (42 USC 290aa4).  Conducted on a periodic basis from 1971 through 1988, and annually since 1990, the NSDUH provides current data on substance use and mental health for the U.S. civilian, non-institutionalized population aged 12 or older.  Since 1999 NSDUH has provided data for each State and the District of Columbia.  Section 505 of the Public Health Service Act requires that these data must be collected annually.

investmentTitle: CMS Healthcare Integrated General Ledger Accounting System (HIGLAS)
analysisResults:
HIGLAS is the Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services Healthcare Integrated General Ledger Accounting System.  It is an integrated accounting system that standardizes and centralizes federal financial accounting functions for all CMS programs.  HIGLAS continues to enhance CMS oversight of all financial operations to achieve accurate, reliable, and timely financial accounting and reporting for all of CMS programs and activities which include:

- Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS)
- Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP)
- Federal Facilitated Marketplace (FFM)
- Administrative Program Accounting (APA) 
         - Medicaid and Childrens Health Insurance Program (CHIP) grants
         - Part C Managed Care 
         - Part D Prescription Drug
         - Federal payroll, contracts, grants, travel, and myriad of other activities
         - Innovation Payment Contractor (IPC) 

HIGLAS is one of the largest accounting systems in the world and its complexity increases every year.  It currently includes CMS financial and budget systems of record, as well as the business intelligence reporting applications that support the Agencys $1.6 trillion in outlays per year.  HIGLAS supports over 147 million Medicare and Medicaid Beneficiaries, processing an average of 4.5 million Medicare claims each day totaling more than $1.5 billion. agencyName: Department of Health and Human Services
analysisResults:
The Import Trade Auxiliary Communication System (ITACS) is a web-based portal for use by the import trade community which was implemented to improve communication between FDA and the import trade community. ITACS allows the import trade community to check the status of FDA-regulated entries and lines, submit entry documentation electronically, submit availability information electronically for those lines targeted for FDA exam, and check the estimated laboratory analysis completion dates for lines which have been sampled. This allows FDA’s import field staff to focus more on entry review and compliance decision-making by reducing the number of calls received from trade to check on entry/line status as well as eliminating the review and handling of paper documents.  User assessment is provided on an ongoing basis via the ITACS Support email box. External users can report issues, and/or suggest system enhancements. As ITACS is used by external (import trade, not FDA) users a formal user survey is not feasible.  ITACS allows the import trade community to check the status of FDA-regulated entries and
lines, submit entry documentation electronically, submit availability information electronically for those lines targeted for FDA exam, and check the estimated laboratory analysis completion dates for lines which have been sampled by FDA. ITACS account management functionality enables the electronic distribution of Notices of FDA Action via email and as pdf downloads from within ITACS. It also allows account holders to view the details of specific information requests. TAC is a relatively simple web-based access point for trade to submit documents and check status of entry filings. Cost of modernization or complete replacement with another system or application like cloud-based solutions would not be cost beneficial to OII. It is recommended that OII continue to sustain the system as is since efforts are underway for a comprehensive review of imports systems with intent on modernization. Since no concrete plan has emerged from these discussions, it would be beneficial for current sustainment efforts continue until actionable plans emerge from modernization discussions.

analysisResults:
Recommendation is continuation of the IT investment.  CMS launched the CCW in 2005 in response to the Medicare Modernization Act of 2003 (MMA), Section 723 which outlined a plan to improve the quality of care and reduce the cost of care for chronically ill Medicare beneficiaries. The essential objective of the plan established a research data warehouse containing Medicare and Medicaid claims data, Assessments data, and Part D Prescription Drug Event data, linked by beneficiary, across the continuum of care, more readily available to healthcare researchers. The CCW provides the data for the research needed to identify areas for improving the quality of care provided to chronically ill Medicare beneficiaries and ways to reduce program spending.  During 2020, the increased demands for COVID-19 related data heightened the capabilities CCW has to quickly respond and deliver relevant data to healthcare researchers.  The CCW environment continues to provide customers with the needed functionality and performance required to conduct their research. Users from CMS, CMS contractors, Federal agencies and external researchers use CCW data for research.  Data includes sources such as Part A and B Claims and Eligibility/Enrollment Files, EDB, CME, Denominator, T-MSIS, Alpha MAX, Part D, Assessments (MDS, OASIS, LTC, Swing Bed, IRF-PAI), Provider (NPPES, PECOS), Encounter, MedPAR, LDS, and PUF.
The implementation and continued extension of the cloud-native alternative analytic environment established in 2020 will bring innovative analytic capabilities for users.   Completion of the migration to the AWS cloud-hosted environment provides cost reduction opportunities through decommissioning the data center at RagingWire and backup data center at LightEdge.  Additional opportunities to engage users with cloud-based data transfers will reduce or eliminate the costs of physical shipments.

analysisResults:
MPSM has made continuous strides towards modernization since 2018. The MPSM program is a coordinated effort among various product development, support, maintenance, and testing teams. The FY2024 Program Objectives reflect the importance of implementing dental claims processing capabilities in a modern system, as well as continuing modernization efforts, apart from dental, that will advance the program toward reaching its overall objectives of making data available timely, reliable, and increasing the responsiveness of claims processing systems.

In November of 2022, CMS announced that it will expand Medicare coverage to include additional medically necessary dental procedures when they are tied to certain procedures and outcomes. The four Dental Teams: Dental Claims Ingestion, Dental Beneficiary Validation, Modern Claim Adjudication Development Services (MCADS), and Multi-Carrier System (MCS)/Healthcare Integrated General Ledger Accounting System (HIGLAS) worked on delivering the Minimum Viable Product (MVP) that can receive, ingest, adjudicate, and pay 100% of dental claims received. On July 1st, 2024, the acceptance and processing of electronic dental claims was enabled. In addition, other major milestones were achieved such as  Electronic Data Interchange (EDI) enrollment opened and 837D Companion Guides were published.

In addition to the delivery of new software, the MPSM team is learning and applying modern system development principles and practices. Collaborative and iterative agile methodologies, which involve frequent reviews of progress that allows us to adjust and adapt based on continual feedback. Product management principles to deeply understand business and policy drivers, so that we make informed and prioritized recommendations for what to build and why. Human-centered design principles to understand the need and perspectives upstream, downstream, and real-time users and consumers of our systems.

The MPSM team has recently started several workgroups to discuss the strategic direction of the program. The workgroups revisited the MPSM strategy this fall and are working on the details of the revised roadmap. The revised strategy and roadmap are expected in January/February of 2025.

The BMISS Investment Manager (IM) manages and monitors the overall IT budget, schedule and risk for the overall portfolio and all BMISS projects to ensure they achieve business needs cost effectively.  The IM reports on projects monthly via HRSA’s Portfolio Management Tool (Folio) and openly discusses questions or concerns with the CPIC Manager and the Project Management Office and other critical partners across HRSA.  To meet OMB requirements, the IM reviews projects to make certain reportable milestones are provided and occur in a period of time no longer than 6 months of the previous milestone.  This provides HRSA with the ability to enact the necessary governance for identifying which projects should continue, which should end, and whether adjustments are needed. 

Additionally, DBO leadership and the IM meet weekly with the software development team to discuss the status of every project, proactively identify any significant issues or risks and planned corrective action to ensure the IT investment achieves approved budget, schedule and cost baselines.  The team continues to meet monthly to focus specifically on the Key Activities and Deliverables identified in each of the BMISS Platform call orders and vendor responses. analysisResults:
HIGLAS, a mission critical system, enables CMS to manage program accounting for its business operations.  On an average, HIGLAS processes 4.5 million claims daily accounting for approximately $1.4 trillion in outlays per year thus making it the largest Oracle Federal Financials System.  HIGLAS continues to enhance CMS oversight of financial operations, in order to achieve reliable, auditable, timely financial accounting, and reporting for CMS programs and activities.

The HIGLAS effort has significantly improved the ability of CMS/HHS to perform accounting transactions.  These improvements and benefits attributable to HIGLAS include reduced costs due to elimination of redundant individual Medicare financial record systems, improvements in automated Medicare debt collection/referral activities, creation of audit trails for every Medicare transaction/payment/claim in HIGLAS, improved Medicare financial audit ability, and improved capability for CMS to more systematically and efficiently recover identified Medicare overpayments.  Moreover, HIGLAS implementation has resulted in better internal financial controls across Medicare contractor operations.  Implementation of HIGLAS has a significant and positive impact on the amount of additional interest earned (saved) in the Medicare Trust Funds.  In addition, HIGLAS provided the capability for CMS and HHS to achieve compliance with the Federal Financial Management Improvement Act (FFMIA) of 1996.

The operational success of HIGLAS is instrumental to CMS and the following programs:  Medicare Fee-for-Service (FFS), Medicare Secondary Payer (MSP), Federal Facilitated Marketplace (FFM), and Administrative Program Accounting (APA).

The implementation and continued expansion of the cloud-native analytic environment established in 2020 will continue to bring innovative analytic capabilities for users.  Completion of the migration to the AWS cloud-hosted environment in 2022 provides cost reduction opportunities through decommissioning the data center at RagingWire and already realized elimination of the backup data center at LightEdge. The vast majority of all Violation Notices written by OLE officers are processed through the LEMIS Violation Notice module.  All OLE special agents track investigative activities through the LEMIS Activity Reporting module. This level of requirements compliance is accomplished by providing reports, asset management functionality, and services from the EFMSS applications and interfaces with core Maximo (FMSS). Through efficient reporting, facility data requests can be met in a timely and accurate manner. EFMSS is the system of record for all NPS constructed asset data.
Customer Results: As indicated in the recent customer survey, EFMSS customers are generally satisfied with the overall services the EFMSS provides at the many diverse layers of customer consumption and use. Survey responses indicate that the recent investments made in DME were successful in providing enhanced user experiences and supporting new and needed functionality. Although customer satisfaction in most categories improved, opportunities exist to improve operational performance and improve customer satisfaction.
Financial Performance: While the negative cost variance at which EFMSS operated in 2023 is significant and includes cost savings, part of the variance includes deferred acquisitions and unexpectedly vacant positions. Investments in DME appear to be yielding results in terms of system improvements resulting in efficiencies and cost savings. The EFMSS provides constructed asset data, and enables NPS facility related strategic planning, analysis, and execution to be efficient, defensible, and reviewable. EFMSS greatly contributes to the understanding and management of the total cost of facility management across the NPS. EFMSS data provides a sound basis for understanding asset management needs to make hard management decisions when distributing dollars across the various park priorities for all NPS divisions, including and beyond the PFMD.
Innovation: PFMD annually reviews customer requirements and solicits input to inform future requirements for EFMSS. In addition to the gathering customer inputs, PFMD reviews utilization trends and the technological state of network infrastructure. Based on these analyses, recommendations are made for modifying the system to accommodate customer requirements, changes, and necessary infrastructure changes. These recommendations are prioritized based on impact to mission success and safety, risk of service interruptions due to failure, cost, customer demand, technology improvements, and schedule.

The USGS has a mandate to provide base topographic information to the Nation, including the needs of its own scientific programs and those of other Federal agencies. The mission is consistent with the Office of Management and Budget Circular A-16, "Coordination of Surveying, Mapping, and Related Spatial Data Activities." Circular A-16 requires the USGS to lead the Nation in providing and maintaining a common set of base information and is the Federal agency leader for elevation, hydrography, orthoimagery, and geographic names. The USGS is providing the national leadership to develop and maintain TNM. TNM supports National Critical Infrastructure assets by being the (1) guarantor of national data completeness, consistency, and accuracy, (2) catalyst and collaborator for creating and stimulating partnerships, (3) integrator and certifier of basic geospatial data from other participants, (4) owner and data producer of content for TNM when no other suitable and verifiable source for those data exist, and (5) leader in the development and implementation of national geospatial data standards. The National Map Reengineering Project describes the plan to provide the information technology and infrastructure to implement the vision of TNM in order to meet national needs for basic geospatial data.

investmentTitle: BOR - CRSP ICS (Colorado River Storage Project Industrial Control Systems)
analysisResults:
The CRSP ICS has met the needs of the stakeholders with some difficulty during FY23. Due to the aging equipment within the CRSP ICS SCADA subcomponent, intermittent outages were observed. Additional data communication and transmission issues between BOR and Western Area Power Administration (WAPA) provided additional gaps in goal achievement, requiring local physical control and manual data calculations to maintain HDB integrity. Additionally, contracted external specialized SCADA technical support was identified as necessary resulting in a significant increase in funding requirements for the contracted support. 

The Authorization to Operate (ATO) was revoked for the CRSP ICS investment on August 10, 2022, because of existing security risks within the ICS systems which were not addressed. All components of the CRSP ICS business investment are subject to this action of a denied ATO. The SCADA upgrade contract (awarded in Jan. of 2018) was cancelled for convenience due to excessive contractor delays. A new path for upgrading the SCADA subcomponent has been identified and efforts to move this forward are being expedited. The expected completion date is tentatively scheduled for FY25-26. This upgrade, when finished, will completely modernize the system. All existing services such as remote operations of facilities, electronic delivery of water, power reports, and data exchange with WAPA will continue. Additional improvements such as ad-hoc reporting availability from an external data historian and improved fault tolerance from a distributed architecture will also be realized. There are currently many un-remediated documented FISMA compliance deficiencies of the legacy SCADA system. These deficiencies documented as POA&Ms, have become delayed resulting in the recent revocation of the Authority to Operate for the CRSP ICS. These POA&Ms are the result of a DHS system review in 2017, OIG audit in 2019, and Critical Vulnerability Assessments in 2020 and 2022. Remediation actions have been put into place to address the majority of the delayed POA&Ms which resulted in the conditional restoration of the CRSP ICS ATO on September 30, 2023, with requirements that must be met by March 31, 2024.  

Currently the CRSP ICS investment is on track to meet budgetary performance goals. Additional actions could be leveraged to communicate and coordinate unexpected costs and variances to ensure investment budget is accurate and complete for upcoming fiscal years.

analysisResults: The Brady Handgun Violence Prevention Act of 1993 required the United States Attorney General to establish the National Instant Criminal Background Check system (NICS). this name check-only system is utilized by Federal Firearms Licensees (FFL) to conduct background checks on potential buyers of firearms. The New Core Financial Management System (NCFMS) is the financial system of record for the U.S. Department of Labor (DOL) and supports the Office of the Chief Financial Officer (OCFO) mission to uphold strong financial management principles and accountability by providing timely, accurate, and reliable financial information. DOL must comply with current federal mandates including both G-Invoicing and Executive Order 14028(also known as the Cyber XO). G-Invoicing is a U.S. Department of Treasury mandated solution for use by federal agencies as a solution to improve the quality of Inter-Governmental Transactions (IGT) by establishing a common federal standard and integrate Treasury accounting with those of federal agencies financial systems. As part of the G-Invoicing effort, the business process for DOL Working Capital Fund must be updated to work with the Treasury G-Invoicing solution. Similarly, Executive Order (EO) 14028, Improving the Nation Cybersecurity mandates enhanced data encryption standards implementation which requires additional software and hardware updates to the current technical architecture, standard operating procedures, policies, and procedures. The team is enhancing encryption for both data-at-rest and data-in-transit across the NCFMS technical stack to meet the ever-evolving Zero trust Architecture requirements as per the EO guidelines and FISMA requirements. Similarly, to address Section 508c compliance requirements and planned deprecation of support for certain browser components by major web browsers, NCFMS must modernize the front-end framework. The Framework Modernization project also provides better user experience by incorporating user feedback for improvements to usability, accessibility, availability and compliance of NCFMS technologies.

The investment also continues to proactively evaluate and integrate emerging technologies to enhance financial management processes. New capabilities are incorporated into existing systems and workflows in a way that minimizes operational disruption while maximizing long-term value. This adaptability ensures ongoing alignment with industry best practices and evolving agency requirements. A key forward-looking initiative within the investment is the development of a new fee billing engine. This capability is being engineered to support next-generation nuclear energy initiatives by delivering flexible, tiered licensee fee pricing models. The fee billing engine will position the NRC to accommodate advanced reactor technologies and innovative licensing frameworks while maintaining equity, transparency, and fiscal accountability. 
The Financial Services IT investment maintains a strong operational posture, continuously modernizes its capabilities, and ensures that financial systems remain secure, efficient, and mission-ready. Through these efforts, the investment upholds its central role in enabling the NRC to fulfill its regulatory mission in a dynamic and rapidly evolving landscape.

Section 131 of the Immigration Act of 1990 (Pub. L. 101-649) amended INA 203 to provide for a new class of immigrants known as “diversity immigrants”. The Act makes available approximately 50,000 permanent resident visas annually to persons from countries with low rates of immigration to the U.S. Applicants to the program must meet strict eligibility requirements.

Due to the above mandate, the eDV system get enhanced with the annual updates to the verbiage and date changes to continue to adhere to the mandates.

DIS is carefully maintaining a consistent operational profile while the program is continuing to develop and build major capabilities and the user base continues to expand. Consistent with OMB guidance that requires all steady state projects, including the steady state portion of Mixed Life Cycle investment, to be reviewed periodically, DIS is evaluated by the following metrics: customer satisfaction based on their deployment experience, direct user support, and strategic and business results. Customer Satisfaction - Users of the DIS system continue to be satisfied with the performance of the application and support from the DIS team. As FY2021 is focusing on the deployment of the DIS performance management module globally, the survey response is collected to reflect their DIS onboarding experience. Survey responses over the past 12 months have rated DIS service with an average 4.55 out of 5.0, exceeding the target metric of 3.0. In addition, the system availability metric maintained an average 99.95% uptime. Direct User Support - DIS has received over 3000 tickets in FY2021. The DIS help desk was able to resolve each high priority ticket within the service level agreement of 24 working hours. Strategic and Business Results - From the business perspective, DIS is experiencing some challenges in meeting the system decommission target of siloed monitoring and evaluation systems used by various Agency Missions. The COVID-19 outbreak and USAID's operational response have shifted priorities throughout the Agency including the Office of the CIO. Missions and DIS have deprioritized tasks related to sunsetting in-use M&E systems and the full transition to DIS, resulting in delays to decommissioning these third-party systems.

Based on overall customer satisfaction, business and strategic results, current financial performance, and continuous innovation; USAID's financial system Phoenix has successfully met the Agency's business needs as outlined in the Operational Analysis for FY2021. For customer service, the Phoenix team tracks user satisfaction via User Surveys with a target of 78% overall satisfaction. For the March 2021 survey, 85% of Phoenix users surveyed are satisfied with Phoenix. 78% of users surveyed are satisfied with Phoenix system performance, including its load times and online availability. Finally, 82% of users surveyed were satisfied with the level of support provided for users of Phoenix including materials as well as help desk support. Phoenix has been increasing financial operational effectiveness for business strategic results. The Phones team tracks three metrics: percentage of help desk tickets resolved with a target of 90%, percentage of Reports uptime with a target of 98%, and percentage of Phoenix uptime with a target of 100%. For FY2021, the average percentage of help desk tickets resolved within 32 hours was 98%. For Phoenix reports uptime, the average percentage of days when financial reports are available to users has been 100%. Finally for Phoenix uptime, the average percentage of planned uptime during which Phoenix is available to users has been 100%. In addition, USAID has successfully made incremental investments to automate and streamline financial management processes. The Phoenix team tracks the percentage of critical incidents that are responded to within three hours with a target of 100%. The response to critical incidents averaged to 100%. In terms of innovation, the Phoenix technical operations team is utilizing the Jenkins CI/DC tool as part of their DevOps approach to delivery. This tool allows the operations team to deploy faster, outside business hours and allows for less lead time for code fixes and also frees up technical resources to perform high-value work instead of focusing on environment availability and deployment. The Phoenix team has developed a disaster recovery plan which allows the transfer of data between two separate server locations with no more than a day's downtime which supports USAID continuity operations in times of disasters. Finally, Phoenix continues to adhere to Federal requirements and guidelines including switching from using DUNS to UEI for SAM.gov, evolving DATA Act requirements, among others.

Strategic and Business Results: The DIS program has been deployed to nearly 80% of targeted Operational Units (OU's) across the Agency. DIS program's performance metrics track the user satisfaction score, help desk ticket resolution time, system availability, and overall intended use for performance reporting in order to evaluate the program's health and operational effectiveness. The DIS team has maintained system availability and critical issue resolution at nearly 100%. This vision will guide future DIS development activities based on the attainability of highest value to the Agency and other stakeholders. Innovation: DIS aims to streamline the Agency's performance management data to the best extent possible, thus, the DIS Program continues to drive functional improvements with each release. Enterprise Architecture: The DIS Program has no plans for major architectural changes in the near future. Security and Privacy: DIS is working to close outstanding POA&Ms while looking to extend the current ATO for two additional years given the POA&Ms are fully addressed.

SCINet’s users comprise scientists and technicians from across ARS’s research programs, their collaborators, and researchers from other USDA agencies (most prominently the Forest Service). SCINet program staff use a variety of methods to assess user needs and concerns and ensure that SCINet resources are meeting the needs of the user community. These include:
• Virtual visits to research locations and research units to provide information about and guidance for using SCINet resources, assess user needs, and gather user feedback.
• Governance committees with members who are system users, which gives SCINet’s user community a central role in steering the evolution of SCINet’s infrastructure to ensure it meets the changing needs of agricultural research.
• Online surveys of current and potential SCINet users to assess user’s needs and satisfaction and identify unmet scientific computing needs.
• One-on-one meetings with researchers and research teams to learn more about particular use cases, consult on best practices and use of SCINet resources, and identify opportunities for infrastructure improvement.
• Facilitation of working groups that focus on particular areas of scientific computing and that provide regular opportunities to engage with the user community and identify opportunities for improvement.
• Review of support ticket requests to identify trends in user questions and challenges.
• Detailed analyses of SCINet computational resource usage data to identify trends in utilization across ARS’s research programs, research units, and geographic locations.
Over the last three years, SCINet has seen steady and substantial growth in the size of its user community and utilization across ARS research programs and locations. SCINet is now used extensively across all ARS national research program areas and by almost all research locations.

US Army Corps of Engineers, Business Systems Modernization (BSM) Assessment, Business Case Analysis

Migrating from the current on-premises, USACE IT-supported network, and server environment to the target Alternative 7 SaaS solution in the cloud will result in the following IT-focused benefits:
- Increased security. Enhanced stability and improved performance due to CSP/SaaS - no more reliance on internal USACE network and server environment and the applications Increased security. 
- Enhanced Protection of personally identifiable information (PII) and construction data are secure.
- Expanded trust and credibility with customer base resulting from greater transparency in IT support, improved communications with the customer, improved user experience, and created better alignment with customer needs.
- Future-proofing - new technologies and continuous modernization process will provide greater flexibility and adaptability to a rapidly changing IT environment.

The product Procore has documented results from similar use cases across the Construction Management industry. The following are categories and statistics that show a marked improvement when adopting a fully integrated CM/CA tool like Procore.

Improve Efficiency
- Process Change Orders quicker - Procore reports an average of 4.5 days saved
- Process RFIs quicker - Procore reports an average of 3 days saved
- Process Submittals quicker - Procore reports an average of 3 days saved
Reduce Risk
- Reduce Risk by enhancing project visibility - Procore reports an average of 84% reduction
Reduce Costs
- Increase in projects managed with same resources -Procore reports an average of 29% increase
- Increase in construction volume managed with same resources - Procore reports an average of 32% increase
- Increase in the confidence of meeting goals with the same resources - Procore reports an average of 83% increase
Resolve issues in real-time
- Reduces time to resolve punch list items - Procore reports an average of 40% reduction
Streamline communication
- Track labor productivity - Procore reports an 80% increase
- Field crew's ability to document site issues - Procore reports a 63% increase
- Improved communications between the field and office - Procore reports a 61% increase

INSTITUTE FOR DEFENSE ANALYSES: An Assessment of the Resident Management System (RMS) for the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers. 

The IDA team recommends: 
- Move to a commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) cloud-based CM solution. This option would shift RMS away from a government-owned-and-operated solution to a vendor-developed, vendor-managed solution. With a COTS solution, the vendor maintains and supports the software. Some of the leading CM vendors are used in the Federal sector and have DoD-approved cloud offerings. Most solutions contain a mobile application for QA/QC, integrate with Autodesk and ArcGIS, and are built around industry standards making it easier to exchange data with construction contractors.
- Conduct an Analysis of Alternatives (AoA) of CM tool suites. RMS is the system of record for CM. The IDA team conducted a market survey and found several leading COTS products that fit USACE's unique CM needs. Some of the COTS products identified in the market survey are already in use in the USACE, DoD, or the Federal Government and could likely be obtained through existing contracts. Before any Request for Proposal can be made, the RMS PO should conduct an AoA to compare the operational effectiveness, suitability, and
life-cycle cost of alternative CM solutions that satisfy the established RMS capabilities.  

The stability of RMS provides USACE with the opportunity to shift to a commercial, cloud-based CM solution with little disruption. Moving to a COTS solution will require effort, but RMS can continue to operate until the shift is made. COTS solutions are already used or tested in the districts and their lessons learned should be used in selecting a COTS product.

The Access to Archival Databases (AAD) resource, deployed in 2003, is a publicly accessible application developed under NARA’s Electronic Records Archives (ERA) program.  AAD is designed and built to provide the public with access to a certain type of electronic records in NARA’s holdings, which are databases that contain record-level information.  The unique feature of AAD is that it makes the records in these raw data files available to the public in a user-friendly format that includes field titles and meanings for coded values.  With AAD, researchers can create custom searches for specific files, run keyword searches across all or a subset of files, view full records with coded values interpreted, and download search results in a comma-delimited format.  This allows researchers to access these records who otherwise would not be able to do so because of the level of data processing needed to use raw data files. AAD is the only ERA environment that has information which is readily accessible to the public without an approved account and therefore is a critical component of providing user-friendly access to these types of records.  There are currently 277 million data records from 65 series available for searching in AAD.  
Currently AAD has no formal mechanism or standard method of evaluating end-user/customer satisfaction.  However, AAD collects statistics on the number of queries run that reflect customers are using the resource.  From FY22 through FY23 there was an average of 2.8 million search queries run on AAD or a daily average of 7,800 search queries.  For the first two quarters of FY24, there is a daily average of 6,678 search queries for a total of the daily average of search queries for a total of 1.2 million searches. ADRRES TS 
ADRRES systems began over 20 years ago and was intended to support the declassification process for paper records.  ADRRES currently provides automated support for systematic declassification review and the processing of FOIA/MDR requests for classified Federal and Presidential records.  For the systematic declassification process, ADRRES supports review, case tracking, capturing metadata, tracking statistics, and reporting.  For the FOIA/MDR process, the system supports case tracking, review, scanning of documents into a case file, consultation with equity agencies, electronic redaction, release of declassified records, tracking statistics and mandatory reporting for legal and regulatory requirements. ADRRES is a custom-built information system based on the HighView 3 SDK and the Microsoft Active Server Pages (ASP.Net) framework.ADRRES is operational and requires ongoing operational support and maintenance. NARA has physically separate instances of ADRRES. The first two instances are used for processing Federal and Presidential records and are housed in a vault at the Archives II facility, one is classified at the TS/RD level and the other is classified  at the Sensitive Compartmented Information (SCI) level, The third instance is classified at the SCI level is used to process Legislative records at the Archives I facility in Washington, DC.
The analysis found the need for enhancement to modernize the system from the existing legacy HighView and Oracle environment to a new technology and platform.  Ongoing development for bug fixes and enhancement are dependent on the funding availability.  Main risks must be considered when considering modernization in the future are data migration on ADRRES TS. The results of the Program’s survey, below, were found to be feasible to improve to the system:
Modernize the production, development, test and integration environments.
Upgrade to a product and process that meets the needs of modern records in a secure and user friendly format. 
Tech upgrades with advanced technology and a solution for redacting tools without binding to the only choice of HighView platform.  
Upgrade the system to support review and processing of electronic records.
Continuous Operations and Maintenance to support the system without interruption of performance and meet the customers’ expectations.
Leverage cloud-base to enhance the current system. 
Fully implement modernized ADRRES to provide efficiency search features.
